status: preliminary engineering concept - prototype and vendor gates required
description: A low-profile welded dry chamber around the AM59 electronics section. The exact OEM heatsink and fan bank remain in a floodable, freely drained wet bay outside the IP66 dry boundary. Residual dry-side heat is rejected passively through a finned service door.

coordinate_system.x: AM59 airflow direction, fan inlet at -X and exhaust/connectors at +X
coordinate_system.y: wet side at -Y, dry service side at +Y
coordinate_system.z: up; preliminary rotator reference plane is Z=0
coordinate_system.note: The provisional axis passes 25 mm into the dry chamber so the complete empty assembly balances about it. It is a mass/CG datum only; no mast adapter, rotator mounting pattern, or load-transfer hardware is designed.

source_control.note: The supplied AM59 PDF controls electrical, environmental, nominal mass, and outline callouts. The supplied STEP controls the packaging keep-out used by this CAD. The PDF says a modular form is available for OEM integration but gives no modular thermal/mechanical interface; it also calls this AM59 model an AM10-series amplifier in the prose, an apparent document inconsistency to resolve.

materials.door_gasket: one-piece outdoor EPDM or silicone, final compound and gland by selected seal vendor
materials.amplifier_transition_boot: one-piece molded 50 Shore A EPDM double-lip boot, no field splice
materials.external_hardware: A4/316 stainless outside the dry boundary with isolating washers except at deliberate bond points
materials.finish: chromium-free conversion coat plus UV-stable white high-emissivity exterior powder coat
materials.bonding: masked conductive lands and short tinned-copper braids; final lightning and RF bonding are separate gates

airflow.standard_fan_moisture_rating: Not established. The official datasheet lists IP54/IP68 only as possible custom designs.
airflow.release_requirement: Obtain an AM59-approved moisture-protected fan build (IP68 preferred) and sealed/potted wet-side fan-lead penetrations without reducing the qualified airflow.

electrical_and_thermal.note: The 125 W and 200 W values are engineering estimates inferred from the model-specific electrical limits, not vendor calorimetry. The 10 percent dry-side split is deliberately conservative but must be measured.

dry_enclosure.pressure_boundary_note: Continuous welds only. No stitch seams, ordinary drains, filtered openings, structural through-bolts, connector holes, vent hole, or mounting holes are included.
dry_enclosure.fabrication_note: Finish-machine or locally machine the amplifier-boot and door-gasket lands after welding. Verify wall and flange flatness before seal installation.

amplifier_boundary.wet_backer: None. Blind studs/bosses welded to the dry bulkhead react the clamp load without holes or hardware on the wet face.
amplifier_boundary.fastener_thread: M5 A4-80 into blind captive hardware outside the gasket opening
amplifier_boundary.seal_strategy: The boot outer flange is axially compressed to the welded bulkhead. Its continuous double inner lip is radially compressed onto a verified uninterrupted AM59 case band. This avoids using the narrow OEM mounting flange as the annular wall seal, but the AM59 thermal wall, fasteners, fan-lead path, and any heatsink-to-electronics joint on the wet side must also be proven leak-tight against an internal bypass into the dry-side electronics.
amplifier_boundary.service_strategy: Remove the dry door and DIN carrier, disconnect internal AM59 connections, release both clamp frames, then withdraw the amplifier toward the wet side. Replace the transition boot after disturbance.
amplifier_boundary.release_gate: A physical AM59 must prove a continuous, dimensionally controlled, coating-compatible seal band with no cover seam, fastener, label, connector, fan lead, or leak path beneath either lip.

service_door.fastener_thread: M5 captive screws into blind replaceable inserts outside the gasket line
service_door.compression_stops: Machined or bonded hard stops set final gasket squeeze; final dimensions depend on the selected seal.
service_door.door_note: The external vertical fins are passive heat-rejection and stiffening features. They remain open to natural convection beneath the solar shield.

din_service_space.service_strategy: A removable carrier is accessed directly after the +Y door is removed. Put future heavy power/protection components on the lower rail and low-mass controls on the upper rail.
din_service_space.excluded: No future power, control, protection, terminal, connector, or wire-routing parts are selected or modeled.

wet_weather_shroud.classification: non-pressure-boundary wet bay; floodable and freely drained
wet_weather_shroud.drainage: Both large downward-facing end openings are primary drains. Hem and stiffener details must not create water traps. The central splash floor receives positive falls toward both openings in production.
wet_weather_shroud.weather_note: The hood suppresses direct rain and solar loading but is not the IP boundary. Wet-side heatsink, fans, guards, coatings, fasteners, and fan wiring must tolerate condensation and incidental spray.

sun_shield.note: Freely ventilated shield only. It does not form an ingress boundary and must not bridge water to the service gasket.

thermal_budget.note: The dry-side estimate includes only heat crossing or generated inside the IP boundary. The OEM heatsink heat and its 1.8 W fan power are rejected directly in the wet bay.

selected_passive.capacity_definition: 51.75 W at 18.8 K dry-air rise using preliminary UA=2.75 W/K
selected_passive.maintenance: visual cleaning of external door fins

seifert_3050303.disposition: Thermally adequate but unnecessary. It adds mass, electrical rejection, wind area, condensate risk, and cost.

seifert_family_reference.source_basis: Supplied AutomationDirect/Seifert catalog; capacity and power are rated at 35 C internal and ambient.

common.mounting: recessed; external mounting kits available; roof mounting prohibited
common.condensate: tray/drain accessories are optional and may be required

seifert_family_reference.disposition: The 3050303 is the smallest family member that brackets the 51.75 W margin load at positive dry-to-ambient delta-T, but passive cooling avoids its mass, parasitic power, condensate system, cutout, and cost.

hoffman_te09_family.rating: IP65; unshrouded and stainless-shrouded variants Type 4X, painted shroud Type 4
hoffman_te09_family.disposition: Smallest Hoffman TEC family and thermally plausible at positive delta-T, but still adds mass, 89 W input, condensate/fan controls, cost, and an IP65 component ceiling.

hoffman_te121024010.rating: Type 12/3R/4 and IP65; painted shroud is not Type 4X
hoffman_te121024010.disposition: Thermally adequate but cannot support an IP66 assembly claim from its component rating and is much heavier than passive cooling.

hoffman_te162024020.disposition: Grossly oversized for residual dry heat, IP65 only, and strongly adverse to mass, CG, wind area, and power.

hoffman_tx23_air_to_air.disposition: Closed-loop and robust but an order of magnitude larger/heavier than the passive requirement; no local STEP was supplied.

hoffman_filtered_fan_with_type4x_shroud.rating: Type 4/4X system possible with specified fan, filter, and shroud; not a dust-tight closed loop
hoffman_filtered_fan_with_type4x_shroud.disposition: Reject for this assembly. It exchanges humid/dusty outdoor air, requires filter service, and the vendor warns that upward-directed spray can cause ingress.

internal_or_external_fans_only.disposition: Internal recirculation can reduce gradients and an external fan can augment door fins, but neither is credited for the passive safe-state thermal rating.

architecture_trade.name: Exact AM59 straddles a sealed bulkhead; heatsink/fans wet; passive dry chamber
Vendor-authorized amplifier/heatsink separation at a cold-wall flange
architecture_trade.reason: Potentially best production architecture, but the supplied STEP and PDF provide no separable thermal-interface drawing, torque, TIM, flatness, or vendor approval.

architecture_trade.name: Entire AM59 in a ventilated wet bay; separate small dry DIN pod
architecture_trade.reason: The AM59 housing and standard fans have no supplied outdoor/IP rating. An open airflow bay cannot be IP6X for the electronics.

architecture_trade.name: Complete AM59 in a sealed chamber with active closed-loop cooler
architecture_trade.reason: Violates the no-heatsink-inside requirement and penalizes mass, CG, wind area, input power, and cost.

mass_model.future_payload_rule: Place the heaviest future items on the lower rail and as close to Y=0 as wiring bend radii permit.

preliminary_cost.basis: 2026 USD, quantity-one prototype budget excluding AM59, connector/feedthrough hardware, mounting hardware, rotator/mast adapters, and future DIN equipment
preliminary_cost.note: The low midpoint assumes a fabricated prototype boot rather than production mold tooling. Obtain supplier quotes before release.

environmental_design.target: Complete populated assembly IP66 after testing: dust-tight and protected against powerful water jets. No IP67 claim.
environmental_design.dry_boundary: welded shell, service-door gasket, and one-piece AM59 transition boot
environmental_design.wet_boundary: none; OEM heatsink bay is intentionally wet, open, and drained
environmental_design.corrosion: Isolate stainless fasteners from aluminum except intentional bond points; qualify coating damage, salt, UV, cleaning chemistry, and wet-side fan materials.
environmental_design.condensation: No active refrigeration is selected, so deliberate sub-dew-point surfaces are absent. Use conformal coating and humidity monitoring for future electronics, and validate sealed-volume humidity over cycling.
environmental_design.pressure: No pressure vent is designed. Thermal/altitude pressure cycling and door/boot loads are qualification items.

qualification_tests: Dimensional first article: exact AM59 seal-band scan, bulkhead/door flatness, gasket squeeze, clamp torque, and service extraction.
Calorimetry: measure total AM59 dissipation and dry/wet heat split at matched load, maximum qualified duty, reduced voltage, and worst permitted mismatch.
Thermal balance: 45 C ambient, zero wind, production sun shield, 51.75 W margin-adjusted dry load, 181.8 W wet-side load, reduced fan voltage, and all planned future DIN heat simulators.

Airflow commissioning: correlate the three fan curves, measured inlet/exhaust pressure, delivered flow, rain-hood guard loading, and amplifier case map. Require no more than 5 Pa added pressure at the accepted operating point.
Wet-side endurance: moisture-protected fan build, fan leads, heatsink, coatings, and hardware under rain, condensation, freeze/thaw, dust accumulation, and restart.
IEC 60529 IP6X on the complete populated dry boundary with production door, boot, clamp frames, representative sealed blanking plates for future interfaces, and no unapproved temporary sealant.
IEC 60529 IPX6 with the unit in every service orientation and jets directed at door seams, amplifier boot, underside openings, drains, fan side, and all welds.
Production leak screen: correlate a pressure-decay or tracer-gas limit to passing IP6X/IPX6 units; temporarily seal only the intentionally absent future interfaces.
Thermal and pressure cycling across the released storage/operating range, including hot shut-down, cold start inhibit, gasket compression set, altitude transport, and humidity soak.
Corrosion/UV exposure for the actual site environment, coating system, galvanic couples, fan plastics, elastomer, labels, and cleaners.
Shock, vibration, transport, fan imbalance, clamp retention, door/finned-panel fatigue, and rain-hood resonance after mounting loads are defined.
Electrical safety, protective bonding, insulation resistance after wet testing, EMC/EMI, fan-fault detection, and independent RF inhibit before full-power outdoor release.
release_gates: Microwave Amps approval for vertical bulkhead orientation, seal-band contact, clamp load, mounting/support method, warranty, and outdoor wet-side use.

Microwave Amps construction evidence and complete populated wet test proving that the heatsink thermal wall, attachment fasteners, fan-lead route, and any wet-side case joint cannot bypass the transition boot into the electronics or dry chamber; otherwise use a vendor-sealed modular/cold-wall variant or redesign the boundary.
Serial-number-controlled AM59 outline and physical first-article measurement; the PDF/STEP connector-region mismatch remains unresolved.
AM59 calorimetry and case map proving the 200 W severe heat basis, 10 percent maximum dry-side split, and 65 C case target at 45 C ambient.
Moisture-protected fan suffix (IP68 preferred), wet connector/lead sealing, fan life, and unchanged installed airflow approved by Microwave Amps and ebm-papst.
Selected transition-boot supplier gland design, continuous case band, material/coating compatibility, compression tolerances, torque, replacement interval, and IP6X/IPX6 test.
Production rain-hood pressure loss no greater than 5 Pa at the accepted fan operating point and no water traps, ice blockage, recirculation, or exhaust-to-inlet short circuit.
Passive enclosure UA at least 2.59 W/K in zero wind after coating, sun shield, DIN population, wiring, and assembly interfaces; otherwise add external fin area before considering active cooling.
DIN equipment selection rated for the qualified internal temperature and vibration, with actual mass/heat substituted for the 1.5 kg/18 W allowances.
Final structural loads, rotator limits, mount interfaces, horn/cable loads, lightning/bonding scheme, and combined mass/CG/wind analysis.
Future connector ports, RF feedthroughs, pressure vent, mast adapters, and rotator mounting hardware are intentionally absent and require separate design/qualification.
